% Numbers: embedding AUC from results_for_paper.txt §1; judge recall from
% balanced_detection_summary.csv (n = 100 AI items per cell).
\providecommand{\cg}[1]{\cellcolor{hmgreen!#1}}

\begin{table*}[t]
  \centering
  \small
  \begin{tabular}{ll c ccc}
  \toprule
    & & Embedding & \multicolumn{3}{c}{LLM-as-judge AI recall (\%)} \\
    \cmidrule(lr){4-6}
    Register & Condition & CV ROC AUC & Claude & Gemini & DeepSeek \\
    \midrule
    Formal   & Baseline          & \cg{38}$0.754$ & \cg{50}$100$ & \cg{48}$96$  & \cg{24}$47$ \\
             & Human-mimicking    & \cg{38}$0.764$ & \cg{50}$100$ & \cg{50}$100$ & \cg{18}$35$ \\
             & Detector-evasive   & \cg{44}$0.880$ & \cg{50}$100$ & \cg{50}$100$ & \cg{46}$92$ \\
    \addlinespace
    Informal & Baseline          & \cg{48}$0.960$ & \cg{47}$94$  & \cg{40}$80$  & \cg{17}$34$ \\
             & Human-mimicking    & \cg{48}$0.963$ & \cg{36}$73$  & \cg{18}$37$  & \cg{0}$1$ \\

  \caption{Cross-method detectability on the same matched corpus (GPT-5.2 regenerations;
  $n=170$ formal / $1{,}149$ informal pairs for embeddings, $n=100$ AI items per cell for
  the judges). Embedding detectability (higher AUC $=$ more separable) and LLM-judge recall
  (higher $=$ more AI text caught) both measure detectability, yet move in \emph{opposite}
  directions under the detector-evasive prompt: on informal text the classifier's AUC rises
  from $0.960$ to $0.981$ while Claude's and Gemini's recall collapse from $94/80\%$ to
  $38/8\%$. The register ordering also inverts across methods --- embeddings find the informal
  register more separable ($0.96$--$0.98$ vs.\ formal $0.75$--$0.88$), whereas the reasoning
  judges find formal AI text easier to catch (Claude/Gemini $\ge96\%$ in every formal
  condition). Surface- and semantic-level evasion are therefore not equivalent.}
  \label{tab:detection-synthesis}
